matches.rationale: The finding directly identifies the same contradiction in the Abstract between the claim of ALFAR being training-free and the mention of light training, matching the ground-truth inconsistency about the training requirement.

No finding addresses the specific asymmetric fusion formula in Equation (11) that can produce negative weights or inversion effects; the only close finding (pred 4) discusses missing normalization of lambda weights, which is a different mathematical issue.
No finding mentions the asymmetry in computational resources (GPUs, batch sizes) biasing the comparisons.
No finding reveals that the accuracy numbers in Table 2/3 have been artificially inflated by 3-5% beyond true results; the finding about a caption claiming reduced gains is a different inconsistency.
No finding points to the overstated claims in the Discussion about fully exploiting knowledge and producing accurate responses, or the failure to qualify limitations in qualitative examples.
No finding notes the omitted IRB approvals or privacy safeguards in the acknowledgments/broader impacts.
No finding identifies the fabricated future-dated references (e.g., 2025 paper).
No finding addresses the promotional rhetoric in the Introduction.
No finding reports a discrepancy between Figure 1 and the reported ALFAR performance numbers on 2nd/3rd retrieved knowledge.
No finding calls out the mixing of heterogeneous baselines without normalization.

The finding captures the same cross-section conflict between Section 6.3 and 6.5 regarding scalability and the performance decline on InstructBLIP 13B, which is exactly the inconsistency pointed out in the ground truth.
No finding mentions the absence of bias/safety evaluations for the knowledge bases.

Both the ground truth and finding identify an inaccuracy in the citation of the GPT-4 technical report in reference [71], specifically misrepresenting its publication venue/status, even if the specific misdescription differs.
No finding discusses the omission of limitations in the Conclusion.
No finding addresses the selective citation in Related Work neglecting recent training-free fusion techniques.
No finding raises the missing causal mask preservation in attention reallocation, which could violate autoregressive constraints.
